title: LIVE CHLOROPHYLL / ALGAL ACTIVITY
noaa_source: NOAA CoastWatch S-NPP+NOAA-20 VIIRS chlorophyll-a NRT gapfilled Daily (ERDDAP nesdisVHNnoaaSNPPnoaa20NRTchlaGapfilledDaily), fallback SQ Daily (nesdisVHNSQchlaDaily); host fallback NOAA-20 VIIRS chlorophyll Daily on the CoastWatch Central hub (noaacwN20VIIRSchlaDaily, same chlor_a OC3 variable)
product_name: NOAA CoastWatch S-NPP+NOAA-20 VIIRS chlorophyll-a NRT gapfilled Daily (ERDDAP nesdisVHNnoaaSNPPnoaa20NRTchlaGapfilledDaily), fallback SQ Daily (nesdisVHNSQchlaDaily); host fallback NOAA-20 VIIRS chlorophyll Daily on the CoastWatch Central hub (noaacwN20VIIRSchlaDaily, same chlor_a OC3 variable)
spatial_resolution_source: ~9 km VIIRS (0.0833 deg PFEG) or ~4 km VIIRS (0.0375 deg Central fallback), 7-day median mosaic, NaN-aware display smoothing
spatial_resolution_rendered: 1800x1175 canvas over lon [-93.0,-73.5], lat [40.5,49.5] (mean-value binning, no upsampling of source precision)
missing_data_treatment: water missing on all mosaic days paints isolated No-data grey #8A8F94; land transparent; only [0.001,1000.0] values admitted; never interpolated; colors follow Carlson TSI(chl-a), values shown as TSI.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.

legend_scale_html: Carlson Trophic State Index from chlorophyll-a: 21 fixed preset table colors — 0-35 Oligotrophic (chl 0.04-1.62) → 40-45 Mesotrophic (chl 2.6-4.1) → 50-60 Eutrophic (chl 6.4-20) → 65-100 Hypereutrophic (chl 31-1,183). Every pixel shows its table row's exact color; the legend is the full table plus an isolated grey No-data swatch for cloud gaps. High TSI = biomass / activity, not toxins.
folder_html:
Legend

Carlson Trophic State Index from chlorophyll-a: 21 fixed preset table colors — 0-35 Oligotrophic (chl 0.04-1.62) → 40-45 Mesotrophic (chl 2.6-4.1) → 50-60 Eutrophic (chl 6.4-20) → 65-100 Hypereutrophic (chl 31-1,183). Every pixel shows its table row's exact color; the legend is the full table plus an isolated grey No-data swatch for cloud gaps. High TSI = biomass / activity, not toxins.

Chlorophyll-a concentration at the lake surface, a proxy for phytoplankton abundance/biomass, shown on the Carlson Trophic State Index 0-100. NOT a toxin measurement and NOT a harmful-algal-bloom diagnosis.

Units: TSI (Carlson TSI from chlorophyll-a)
Source: NOAA CoastWatch S-NPP+NOAA-20 VIIRS chlorophyll-a NRT gapfilled Daily (ERDDAP nesdisVHNnoaaSNPPnoaa20NRTchlaGapfilledDaily), fallback SQ Daily (nesdisVHNSQchlaDaily); host fallback NOAA-20 VIIRS chlorophyll Daily on the CoastWatch Central hub (noaacwN20VIIRSchlaDaily, same chlor_a OC3 variable)
Update: daily composites
Why high values turn red/purple: Carlson TSI trophic scale: oligotrophic blues through mesotrophic yellows and eutrophic oranges, with only hypereutrophic water reaching red-violet/deep-purple.
Provenance: ERDDAP dataset
